title: H3 Chunk
description: One 4-15 s MiniMax H3 clip of a scene: the anchor keeps the place and positions, up to 5 character sheets and 2 props keep the faces.
pick_when: A clip of a scene built from the place's sheet, up to 5 character sheets and 2 props, so faces and positions hold across clips (the script-to-video skills use it). Not for a single shot from one picture: there H3 All-in-One holds the place and the people better.

labels.211:audio: Voice track (this chunk's slice of the episode audio)

hints: <Picture 1> is the anchor (the place); filled character slots follow as <Picture 2>, <Picture 3>... Call people 'character 1', 'character 2', described by look in the same words every clip.

Prompt blocks, short: GOAL · SCENE (layout, light, time, ambience) · OPENING · SHOTS timed '[0-2s] size, lens, angle → one action → dialogue → move' · STYLE · END STATE · LOCKS. No shape or length words.

One job per picture: '<Picture 2> is character 1: face, hair and clothing only'; a place: 'layout and light only, ignore any people'; a prop: 'shape, material, colour only'. Never a clip's frame as identity.
Identity in words: age, build, the features that tell them apart, what the action needs; logos, small text and key colours said in words. One clear action per beat, camera in plain film words.
Dialogue in quotes, tied to its speaker: character 1 says: "Sign here." Sound is always on: a silent clip says 'No dialogue. No music.' No negative prompt: put short 'No ...' lines in LOCKS.
With a voice track and LIPS FOLLOW AUDIO on, write who speaks when: "character 1 speaks 'line' at 3.2-5.0 s; nobody else's lips move". The voice sample is character 1's only.
Several shots in one clip: give one keyframe per shot plus SHOT CUT FRAMES for frame-exact cuts; without them cuts land up to ~1.5 s off the asked times.
H3 cannot carry on from a clip: the next clip's OPENING restates the last one's end state as present fact, never 'previous'. A board in Extra Reference: its highest panel is where this clip opens.
Too many references: keep what the user named, on-screen speakers' sheets, the place, other people, then props; say in the reply what was left out.
Output is exactly round(24 x DURATION) frames at 24 fps; 480p or 768p, landscape, portrait or square, 4-15 s.
